raw_evidence.quote: PRs will be reviewed by active maintainers, who will provide feedback and request changes as needed. ... Once the PR is approved, the maintainers will merge the PR into the develop branch.
When a release is ready, the release/x.x.x branch will be created, extensively tested and knsv will be in charge of the release process.

licence.rationale: SPDX identifier MIT, read directly from the LICENSE file text ('The MIT License (MIT)', copyright Knut Sveidqvist 2014-2022), independently corroborated by the GitHub API's license.spdx_id field. Note mermaid-cli carries a SEPARATE MIT-licensed copyright line (Tyler Long, 2017-2020) in its own repository per source-mermaid-erd-tooling.json — same licence family (MIT) but a distinct copyright holder, since it is a distinct repository.

governance_model.rationale: No formal GOVERNANCE.md exists (confirmed 404). The documented process is maintainer code review with merge authority, plus a single named individual ('knsv', i.e. Knut Sveidqvist, the original author and copyright holder) who is 'in charge of the release process' and whom maintainers 'request a review from... if necessary.' This reads as maintainer-team-led with a founder/BDFL-adjacent figure retaining release authority, not a foundation-governed or formally chartered community-consensus model, and not single-vendor commercial governance in the sense Prisma or Atlas would be (no company is named as backing the mermaid-js/mermaid core project in this document — contrast with the separate commercial entity 'Mermaid Chart', which sponsors some maintainers but is not documented here as controlling governance).
